text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Portuguese state owes 40 billion escudos to the pharmaceutical sector, the newspaper learns.
- Portugal's insurance premiums grew 30 percent in the first seven months of 1996, compared with the same year-ago period.

- The valuation of Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) is under way and should be ready in October, before the privatisation of the state's 13.2 percent stake, BTA president Alipio Dias tells the paper. ING Barings and Arthur Andersen are carrying out the valuation.

- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus will propose to the cabinet this month two foreign investment projects totalling around 15 billion escudos. The projects are a joint-venture between Ford and the South Korean Halla Group to build a car components factory, and the German group Grohe which wants to open a tap factory.

- Centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa says a possible coalition with the rightwing Popular Party (PP) in the next local authority elections in 1997 will depend on European questions.
- Pulp group Portucel Industrial should return to profit when it raises pulp prices later this year, analysts tell the paper.
